Island_074.secondary_feature: Great halls, turf roofs, megaliths, fortified farmsteads
Island_074.lore_notes: Great Cold North architecture: huge timber frames on stone plinths, steep snow roofs, low protected entrances and communal halls. Foreign masonry is translated into heavier northern forms.

Island_073.terrain_character: Snowy taiga frontier and river valleys
Island_073.secondary_feature: Raised timber houses, covered walks, watchtowers, frontier markets
Island_073.lore_notes: Frost Marches architecture: practical timber construction, raised foundations, deep eaves, enclosed yards and compact market towns. Northern hall traditions become smaller civic buildings.

Island_106.terrain_character: Broken ice coast and exposed rocky shores
Island_106.secondary_feature: Sea forts, beacon towers, wreck-built shelters, enclosed harbors
Island_106.lore_notes: Shattered Ice Coast architecture: stone lower walls, timber upper structures, narrow storm-resistant profiles, heavy shutters and salvaged ship timber.

Island_081.terrain_character: Fertile central lowlands and civic hills
Island_081.secondary_feature: Arcaded plazas, civic halls, gatehouses, formal bridges
Island_081.lore_notes: Crownlands architecture: dressed stone, measured streets, broad arches, courtyards and formal squares. Symmetry, hierarchy and planned urban growth distinguish it from its neighbors.

Island_082.terrain_character: High mountains, ravines and alpine terraces
Island_082.secondary_feature: Bridge-castles, monasteries, cliff stairs, vertical keeps
Island_082.lore_notes: High Kingdom architecture: monumental vertical stonework, narrow towers, buttressed walls, cliff bridges and terraced monasteries.

Island_076.terrain_character: Lake valleys, wooded hills and sheltered meadows
Island_076.secondary_feature: Inns, breweries, covered bridges, lakeside piers
Island_076.lore_notes: Hearthlands architecture: warm timber-and-stone houses, deep porches, broad hearths, gabled inns and dense villages shaped around water.

Island_084.terrain_character: Dense production forest and logging valleys
Island_084.secondary_feature: Sawmills, log bridges, timber halls, forest watchtowers
Island_084.lore_notes: Timberlands architecture: oversized timber frames, exposed joinery, broad roofs, drying lofts and functional towers. Structure is celebrated rather than hidden.

Island_093.terrain_character: Open farmland, canals and orchard belts
Island_093.secondary_feature: Granaries, mills, canal locks, barns, walled orchards
Island_093.lore_notes: Breadbasket architecture: broad farm compounds, long barns, mills, canal warehouses and durable farmhouses shaped by land and water management.

Island_088.terrain_character: Dense harbor district and engineered waterfront
Island_088.secondary_feature: Guild halls, cranes, customs houses, covered markets
Island_088.lore_notes: Grand Exchange architecture: tall mercantile buildings, arcaded quays, warehouse rows and mixed imported materials adapted to dense commerce.

Island_077.terrain_character: Industrial terraces, rail cuts and workshop districts
Island_077.secondary_feature: Machine halls, gantries, utility towers, viaducts
Island_077.lore_notes: Engineer's Reach architecture: brick-and-stone industrial shells, long-span roofs, exposed mechanisms, service gantries and modular workshop bays.

Island_089.terrain_character: Bright coastal terraces and artisan quarters
Island_089.secondary_feature: Courtyard workshops, glazed facades, dye houses, decorative arcades
Island_089.lore_notes: Artisan Coast architecture: patterned facades, colored glass, tile and concrete accents, intimate courtyards and street-facing workshops.

Island_075.terrain_character: Dark forest edge and defensive clearings
Island_075.secondary_feature: Palisaded hamlets, ward towers, fortified farmhouses, ruins
Island_075.lore_notes: Haunted Marches architecture: compact defensive compounds, limited windows, heavy shutters, reused masonry, ditches and watch structures.

Island_087.terrain_character: Wetlands, mangrove channels and unstable marsh ground
Island_087.secondary_feature: Stilt towns, boardwalks, raised storehouses, marsh shrines
Island_087.lore_notes: Blackfen architecture: pile foundations, lightweight upper structures, boardwalk spines, roofed docks and elevated communal buildings.

Island_086.secondary_feature: Dry-stone villages, retaining walls, quarry halls, cliff roads
Island_086.lore_notes: Stone Highlands architecture: massive low walls, deep-set openings, retaining terraces, stepped streets and practical quarry-built civic halls.

Island_083.terrain_character: Mesas, clay gullies and kiln valleys
Island_083.secondary_feature: Brickworks, kilns, shaded courtyards, stepped towns
Island_083.lore_notes: Red Clay Basin architecture: brick, terracotta and packed-earth masses, shallow roofs, shaded arcades and courtyard settlements following mesa shelves.

Island_080.terrain_character: Lagoons, tidal flats and shallow inlets
Island_080.secondary_feature: Fishing villages, tidal warehouses, seawalls, flooded ruins
Island_080.lore_notes: Sunken Coast architecture: stilted quays, raised storehouses, tidal gates, seawalls and houses oriented around boat access.

Island_090.terrain_character: Deep caverns, geodes and ancient subterranean voids
Island_090.secondary_feature: Crystal galleries, cavern bridges, carved halls, geometric ruins
Island_090.lore_notes: Crystal Deep architecture: carved spaces, suspended bridges, precise geometric openings and monumental underground halls with controlled crystal light.

Island_047.terrain_character: Basalt slopes, caldera walls and lava-cut terraces
Island_047.secondary_feature: Foundries, lava channels, blackstone arches, furnace citadels
Island_047.lore_notes: Volcano architecture: thick basalt masonry, vaulted hot-work halls, open lava channels, buttresses and heat-separated courtyards.

Island_097.terrain_character: Coves, cliffs and layered harbor slopes
Island_097.secondary_feature: Freeport docks, taverns, rope bridges, shipyards
Island_097.lore_notes: Pirate Island architecture: opportunistic reuse of ship timber and imported stone, stacked warehouses, narrow alleys and additions built over additions.

Island_102.terrain_character: Volcanic coast, ash fields and portal-industrial enclaves
Island_102.secondary_feature: Portal bastions, blackstone works, furnace districts, causeways
Island_102.lore_notes: Ember Coast architecture: severe blackstone/basalt complexes, protected portal courts, defensible streets and compartmentalized industrial districts.

Island_096.terrain_character: Coral shelf, reef channels and pale coastal terraces
Island_096.secondary_feature: Sea towers, reef gardens, water arches, guardian monuments
Island_096.lore_notes: Sapphire Coast architecture: pale stone, prismarine accents, repeated arches over water, stepped seawalls and monumental marine complexes.

Island_085.terrain_character: Tropical hills, fertile coasts and orchard belts
Island_085.secondary_feature: Veranda houses, raised roofs, farm compounds, colorful waterfronts
Island_085.lore_notes: Isles of Plenty architecture: open structures, deep shade, high ventilated roofs, verandas, light raised foundations and lush courtyard compounds.

Island_095.secondary_feature: Lighthouses, terminals, rail halls, bridge towers, inns
Island_095.lore_notes: Transit Isles architecture: infrastructure-first settlements organized around arrival and departure, with standardized wayfinding despite imported regional styles.

Island_128.terrain_character: Remote fog islands and concealed basins
Island_128.secondary_feature: Observatories, hidden compounds, strange towers, secret entrances
Island_128.lore_notes: Shrouded Isles architecture: sparse footprints, strong silhouettes, concealed access, unusual proportions and selectively abstracted End-inspired forms.

Island_081.settlement_role: Crownlands capital: royal-administrative city, civic center and principal iron/raid complex
Island_081.secondary_feature: Palace-citadel, grand market square, senate/guild hall, monumental gatehouses
Island_081.notes: The formal heart of the archipelago's central civilization. Dense planned city with the strongest expression of Crownlands civic architecture.

Island_062.settlement_role: Crownlands fortress island and naval garrison
Island_062.secondary_feature: Arsenal, barracks, fortified harbor, beacon chain
Island_062.notes: A Crownlands military settlement: same arches and masonry vocabulary as the capital, but thicker walls, tighter streets and fewer decorative civic spaces.

Island_139.secondary_feature: Formal cloisters, record halls, gardens and ceremonial bridge
Island_139.notes: A quieter Crownlands expression. Learned institutions use the same proportional order as the capital but with courtyards, cloisters and landscaped precincts.

Island_076.settlement_role: Hearthlands lake capital and culinary center
Island_076.secondary_feature: Great inn, brewery quarter, covered market, lake promenade
Island_076.notes: Primary Hearthlands town: welcoming, dense, walkable and water-oriented; the region's cultural center for food, brewing and hospitality.

Island_017.secondary_feature: Malt houses, breweries, smokehouses, storage cellars
Island_017.notes: Industrial by Hearthlands standards: production remains embedded in a cozy town rather than becoming a factory landscape.

Island_123.settlement_role: Hearthlands farming villages and estate landscape
Island_123.secondary_feature: Orchards, manor farm, cider press, stone field walls
Island_123.notes: Agricultural satellite with Hearthlands cottages and farmsteads; visually softer and more enclosed than the open Breadbasket.

Island_145.secondary_feature: Covered bridge, ferry hall, boathouses, waterfront inn
Island_145.notes: Connects Hearthlands to Crownlands and Grand Exchange. Imported mercantile details appear, but the town remains distinctly Hearthland in scale and warmth.

Island_030.settlement_role: Small lakeside abbey and pilgrimage village
Island_030.secondary_feature: Bell tower, cloister garden, hillside path, guesthouse
Island_030.notes: A low-intensity cultural island that gives the region breathing room and history rather than another production center.

Island_084.settlement_role: Timberlands forestry capital and primary tree-production ecosystem
Island_084.secondary_feature: Great sawmill, timber guild hall, log port, monumental frame hall
Island_084.notes: The main Wood & Tree island. All tree families belong to the broader Timberlands production system, including the intentional Nether-wood consolidation.

Island_143.secondary_feature: Mill race, log ponds, drying yards, timber warehouses
Island_143.notes: A work-focused Timberlands town where the architecture is dominated by exposed structural frames and production infrastructure.

Island_140.settlement_role: Craft town for carpenters, joiners and builders
Island_140.secondary_feature: Joinery hall, covered workshop streets, furniture yards
Island_140.notes: Shows the refined side of Timberlands culture: the same large timber vocabulary used for craftsmanship rather than raw logging.

Island_108.settlement_role: Minimal settlement; ranger and forester outposts only
Island_108.secondary_feature: Ancient grove, canopy paths, fire lookout
Island_108.notes: Intentionally underbuilt. Preserves the impression that the Timberlands civilization lives within a forest larger than its industry.

Island_109.secondary_feature: Boom chains, cranes, log rafts, warehouse piers
Island_109.notes: Trade-facing Timberlands settlement influenced by Grand Exchange logistics but constructed almost entirely through the region's timber tradition.

Island_012.primary_function: Forestry knowledge / seed and sapling stewardship
Island_012.secondary_feature: Tree library, specimen groves, guild lodge
Island_012.notes: A knowledge center devoted to preserving and propagating the complete tree collection; quieter than the production islands.

Island_117.settlement_role: Managed grove communities and specialist nurseries
Island_117.secondary_feature: Distinct grove districts, propagation yards, small lumber camps
Island_117.notes: Use this island to separate visually unusual tree families into designed ecosystems while keeping the overall Wood & Tree system consolidated in one region.

Island_094.secondary_feature: Tall timber fire tower, ranger hut, signal beacon
Island_094.notes: A small architectural punctuation mark rather than a full town; it should make the forest network feel inhabited and managed.

Island_093.settlement_role: Breadbasket market capital and principal agricultural ecosystem
Island_093.secondary_feature: Great granary, central mill, produce market, canal basin
Island_093.notes: The administrative and market center of large-scale agriculture. Broad farm compounds and water-management infrastructure dominate the landscape.

Island_119.settlement_role: Large farm estates, field villages and compost/moss support
Island_119.secondary_feature: Field grids, barns, windmills, composting yards, irrigation works
Island_119.notes: The region's most openly agricultural island, including the bone-meal/moss loops that support farming across the archipelago.

Island_129.secondary_feature: Watermills, lock gates, grain warehouses, barge docks
Island_129.notes: Where Breadbasket production transitions into trade. Grand Exchange influence appears in warehousing, while the settlement remains organized around canals and mills.

Island_088.settlement_role: Grand Exchange metropolis and principal trade hub
Island_088.secondary_feature: Grand market, guild quarter, customs basin, central warehouses
Island_088.notes: The most cosmopolitan city in the archipelago. It moves goods rather than replacing the processing ecosystems that belong in producing regions.

Island_020.secondary_feature: Warehouse canyons, cranes, sorter halls, freight yards
Island_020.notes: A highly functional commercial island with fewer residences; architecture prioritizes loading access, firebreaks and dense storage.

Island_024.settlement_role: Customs harbor, bonded warehouses and foreign docks
Island_024.secondary_feature: Customs house, quarantine pier, foreign merchants' quarter
Island_024.notes: First contact point for much of the archipelago's maritime trade. Foreign architectural details should be most visible here.

Island_156.secondary_feature: Exchange hall, counting houses, auction court, guild palaces
Island_156.notes: A prestige-commercial satellite of the main city. Less cargo infrastructure, more institutions that organize trade and finance.

Island_077.settlement_role: Engineer's Reach city containing several distinct engineering districts
Island_077.secondary_feature: Machine hall district; test yards; rail/transport works; component workshops; power/utilities quarter
Island_077.notes: Because Engineer's Reach is currently a single-island region, treat it as a dense city-region with multiple internal districts rather than one monolithic factory. Preserve neighborhoods and civic spaces between technical zones.

Island_089.settlement_role: Artisan Coast city containing specialized craft quarters
Island_089.secondary_feature: Glassworks; dye quarter; concrete yards; tile workshops; gallery/market district
Island_089.notes: Because Artisan Coast is currently a single-island region, divide the island into culturally coherent craft districts. Production should read as workshops embedded in an inhabited coastal city, not a centralized industrial plant.
